purpose: benchmark packaging patterns; no third-party executable integration or new default packages
default_policy: retain Nemesis Airplanes.live + minimum receiver, network and hardware tools; selected modules only

distributions.name: SigintOS 2.0 Community Edition
distributions.inventory_basis: publisher's featured software list, not package/SBOM export
distributions.deployment_model: broad all-in-one RF and development workstation; GUI-first with cellular laboratory and server components
distributions.nemesis_impact: keep receiver/ADS-B essentials; optional GUI/DSP; exclude servers and cellular infrastructure from default

distributions.name: DragonOS Resolute R2.2
distributions.inventory_basis: publisher release README and image listing, not inspected ISO files
distributions.deployment_model: large readied-to-use lab image; source-installed code in /usr/src and package-managed components; selected servers deliberately on demand
distributions.published_image_size: 4.0 GB as shown by distributor listing
distributions.nemesis_impact: copy on-demand service and hardware plugin principles, not complete cellular/AI/server workload

distributions.name: Skywave Linux 5.10.0
distributions.inventory_basis: publisher versioned software list, not a package manager snapshot
distributions.deployment_model: radio-listening and aviation-centric environment with lightweight window manager but broad bundled programs
distributions.nemesis_impact: aviation/airband/satellite are compelling opt-in receive-only kits; do not copy entire stack or non-Arch binary packages

distributions.name: Pentoo
distributions.inventory_basis: publisher architecture/about description, not SDR-specific package inventory
distributions.deployment_model: capability bundles via Gentoo overlay, meta-ebuild, USE flags and selectable profiles
distributions.nemesis_impact: adopt selection model through independently reviewed signed-Arch manifests, never import Gentoo overlay into Arch

evaluated_capabilities.reason: basic air traffic and hardware tools; no active RF transmission
multiple overlapping GUI receivers; compare actual runtime/closure before deciding between lightweight and full RF kit
DSP graph ecosystem and transitive dependencies, not a default map requirement
receive-only extensions; packages/repository names must be resolved on Arch before a manifest change
extra SDR/decoder dependencies; no default satellite service
network listeners must be disabled by default and reviewed for authentication/ports
active cellular infrastructure, license/interference/privacy rules; no implicit installation or startup
not needed to render globe or receive ADS-B; avoid unattended listener/services
select exact USB/network SDR backend using hardware evidence rather than every driver
